title: Private control plane: DNS TTL surge + ECMP route churn caused auth flaps during rolling upgrade
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a routine rolling upgrade of the Private control plane (agent and proxy stacks) we observed a spike in DNS resolution failures and authenticated control plane API errors across multiple customer VPCs. Symptoms included CONNECTIVITY errors from agents, token rejection logs in the control plane, and elevated 5xx rates in the control plane API for ~12 minutes. Impact: multi-tenant but isolated to Private deployments in eu-west-1 region with customer-facing agent reconnects and two customer incident escalations. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and longer-term action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-10T02:14Z - Rolling upgrade started for control plane agents in eu-west-1 (canary region).
2026-03-10T02:22Z - First agent reconnects observed; ops alerted by synthetic monitors (agent-heartbeat alert).
2026-03-10T02:24Z - DNS resolution error waterfall begins: control plane reports NXDOMAIN / SERVFAIL spikes for internal service FQDNs used by agents.
2026-03-10T02:27Z - Token-validation failures appear as agents attempt to reconnect; control plane returns 401/403 intermittently for legitimate tokens.
2026-03-10T02:30Z - On-call escalates to SRE/Networking; mitigation: pause rolling upgrade and reintroduce previous agent version to a subset of hosts.
2026-03-10T02:40Z - Short-term mitigation applied: increase resolver retry backoff on agents and extend DNS TTL cache times at proxy layer; system stabilizes around 02:50Z.
2026-03-10T03:00Z - Upgrade resumed with stricter sequencing; no further mass failures observed.
root_cause: A confluence of factors: 1) Upgrade introduced a change in agent DNS query sequencing that caused accelerated cache bypass on short TTLs; 2) Underlying customer VPCs were using ECMP between multiple NAT/egress paths which, during the upgrade, flipped a subset of traffic to an alternate egress that had an out-of-date DNS forwarder/ACL leading to transient SERVFAIL responses; 3) The control plane's auth layer treats transient DNS resolution failure as a token verification error path, which temporarily classified otherwise-valid sessions as unauthorized. In short: DNS instability amplified by ECMP path churn combined with agent-side aggressive cache invalidation caused cascading auth flaps.
mitigations_applied: Paused rolling upgrade mid-flight to prevent further spreading.
Rolled back the agent change that forced immediate DNS cache eviction.
Applied a temporary resolver config to agents to prefer cached responses for known internal FQDNs (increase local TTL to 30s).
Adjusted control plane auth layer to treat DNS lookup failures as transient and retry token verification before returning 4xx to agents.
Coordinated with impacted customers to confirm NAT/egress path stability and validate forwarder configs.
analysis: Why this wasn’t caught earlier: integration tests run in single-path networking topologies and did not include ECMP churn scenarios or stale forwarder behavior. The agent change (smaller cache lifetime and immediate re-query on edge events) was intended to reduce stale endpoints but regressed under multi-egress path conditions. The control plane's token verification logic assumed DNS would be reliable and did not surface transient DNS resolution into a retryable auth path. We lacked a canary gate that simulates multi-egress VPC behavior during upgrades.
action_items: (Owner: Miguel Santos) Implement a canary test that exercises ECMP-style multi-egress behavior in our upgrade CI (simulate multiple NAT/egress paths and forwarder divergence) - due 2026-04-04.

(Owner: Priya Kapoor) Rework agent DNS caching policy: introduce a conservative backoff that prefers cached entries for critical internal FQDNs and avoid immediate eviction on health-check induced re-resolve - estimate 3 pts - due 2026-03-28.

(Owner: Riley Chen) Harden control plane auth path to retry token verification on transient DNS failures with exponential backoff and add observability metrics for 'auth-dns-failures' - estimate 2 pts - due 2026-03-25.

(Owner: Network Eng SWG) Provide a runbook for customers/operators to detect and remediate stale DNS forwarders in ECMP setups; include recommended NAT path sequencing during upgrades - due 2026-04-01.
(Owner: Miguel Santos) Add pre-upgrade validation that probes internal resolvers from multiple egress paths and fail the canary if divergence is observed - due 2026-04-04.
(Owner: Asha Patel) Postmortem doc + customer communication draft for impacted customers and account teams - due 2026-03-16.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Initial incident triage notes. Observed DNS SERVFAIL spikes correlating with agent restarts. Paused upgrade at 02:30Z. Rolling back the immediate cache eviction patch as a stopgap.

2026-03-11 - Miguel Santos: Added detailed packet captures from one impacted VPC showing requests leaving on egress A and responses routed back via egress B where forwarder returned SERVFAIL. Attaching PCAPs and resolver logs to Confluence.

2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor: Ran local sim of agent change with ECMP simulator; reproduced cache bypass followed by authentication flap. Proposing configuration to prefer cached entries for internal hostnames.
2026-03-13 - Riley Chen: Implemented auth-layer retry prototype; verified it prevents 401s in synthetic tests when resolver returns SERVFAIL intermittently. Needs code review before canary rollout.

2026-03-14 - Miguel Santos: Coordinated with two affected customers; both validated no persistent data loss and accepted the proposed mitigations and runbook. Moving ticket to In Progress for implementation of action items.
